import { build } from 'esbuild';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';
const file = process.argv[2] ?? 'src/module.ts';
const r = await build({ entryPoints: [file], bundle: true, minify: true, treeShaking: true,
  format: 'esm', platform: 'browser', target: 'es2022', write: false, metafile: true, logLevel: 'silent' });
const own = Object.entries(Object.values(r.metafile.outputs)[0].inputs)
  .filter(([path]) => !path.includes('node_modules/'))
  .reduce((sum, [, info]) => sum + info.bytesInOutput, 0);
console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`, with the same exports and signatures as before. Type checking is clean for `out/module.ts`, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 2362 bytes (min+gzip) with 97 bytes of my own code.

- **`applyPatch`:** it now uses `merge` from `es-toolkit/object`. Like lodash, it mutates and returns `base` and merges arrays index by index. I checked this by reading the source, not by running it. For JSON inputs within your range, I expect it to match the original.
- **`toTitle`:** it uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. I did not use the core `startCase`, because it lowercases the rest of each word and would turn "HTML" into "Html". The compat version keeps the case, as lodash does. I ran `startCase('id.Height_Url.')` and got `Id Height Url`.
- **`preview`:** it uses `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`, since core has no `truncate`. A 30-character string with `{ length: 24 }` came out as 21 characters plus `...`.

There are no lodash imports left, and no hand-written replacements or adapters.

`lodash` isn't installed in this project, so I couldn't run the original and the new version side by side. The output comparison above is from reading the source and the few spot checks.

I didn't try other import paths to shrink the bundle further.
